title: The Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal C$, let $\mathfrak U=\{U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a covering, and let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal C$. There is a convergent first-quadrant spectral sequence

$$
E_2^{p,q}=\check H^p(\mathfrak U,\underline H^q(F))\Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(X,F),
$$

where $\underline H^q(F)$ is the presheaf $V\mapsto H^q(V,F)$ and $\check H^p(\mathfrak U,-)$ is Cech cohomology with respect to the covering $\mathfrak U$.

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution $F\to I^{\bullet}$ in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ and consider the first-quadrant double complex $D^{p,q}:=C^p(\mathfrak U,I^q)=\prod_{i_0,\ldots,i_p}I^q(U_{i_0\cdots i_p})$, with $d_I$ the Cech differential and $d_{II}$ induced by the resolution; they commute because the Cech differential is natural in the presheaf. Cycles and boundaries of a product of complexes of abelian groups are computed coordinatewise, so $H^q_{II}(D^{p,\bullet})=\prod_{i_0,\ldots,i_p}H^q(\Gamma(U_{i_0\cdots i_p},I^\bullet))$, and by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2) $H^q(\Gamma(V,I^\bullet))=H^q(V,F)$, naturally in $V$; hence $H^q_{II}(D^{p,\bullet})=C^p(\mathfrak U,\underline H^q(F))$ with the map induced by $d_I$ the Cech differential. The first spectral sequence of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] therefore has ${}'E_1^{p,q}=C^p(\mathfrak U,\underline H^q(F))$ and ${}'E_2^{p,q}=\check H^p(\mathfrak U,\underline H^q(F))$, and it converges to $H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Tot}D)$.

Each $I^q$ is injective in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-site-injective-cech-acyclic] the row $D^{\bullet,q}=C^\bullet(\mathfrak U,I^q)$ has $H^0_I=I^q(X)$ and $H^p_I=0$ for $p>0$. So the second spectral sequence of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] has ${}''E_1^{q,p}=0$ for $p>0$ and ${}''E_1^{q,0}=I^q(X)$ with $d_1$ induced by $d_{II}$; hence ${}''E_2^{q,0}=H^q(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet))=H^q(X,F)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2), all other entries vanish, so all later differentials are zero and the abutment filtration of $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ has the single nonzero graded piece ${}''E_2^{n,0}$. Thus $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)\cong H^n(X,F)$, and with Step 1 this is the spectral sequence of the statement.

split_report.summary: Split the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence into the double-complex page calculation and the identification of the total cohomology with sheaf cohomology. Reused the existing general double-complex spectral-sequence node, the general-site injective Cech-acyclicity node, and the localized-site exact restriction node; no new nodes were needed. The source Lean declaration remains sorry-bearing, so this is a split rather than an attachment.

steps.1: proof paragraph: choose an injective resolution and form the Cech double complex; identify the E1 and E2 pages
steps.2: proof paragraph: Cech acyclicity of injectives identifies the total cohomology and the abutment
